children: Rescuers will resume the search on Thursday for 13 workers trapped underground in an illegal gold mine in Indonesia's West Java province, with 13 already confirmed dead, police and rescue authorities said.
In the region of Bogor, south of the capital Jakarta, a total of 26 workers entered the mine on Monday when heavy rains inundated the shaft and left them trapped 100 m (328 ft) underground.
Hengki, West Java's police chief, told Reuters that of the 13 fatalities, six have already been identified. The search would continue on Thursday barring bad weather conditions, he added.
Access to the mine has been made more difficult by the narrow, slippery and dark conditions of the shaft, authorities said.
Indonesia's search and rescue agency said rescuers were focusing on two mine shafts, and were using ropes to gain access, but the 100-metre depth of the excavation complicated search efforts.
Small-scale and illegal mining has caused a series of accidents in Indonesia, where mineral resources are located in remote areas in conditions that are difficult for authorities to regulate.
In January, several miners were killed by carbon monoxide poisoning at an illegal gold mine in the same area, local news outlet Detik reported.
, which runs gold mining operations in the region, said the incident occurred at an unauthorised mine and was not part of its operations.
